title: Prism Labs — Porting Sprint Kickoff (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood)
next_steps: Jordan to share SOC2 + KMS integration docs and console walkthrough recording
Sana to run a 48-hour perf/cost baseline on Prism prompt set and share results
Prism to provide three canonical prompt templates and daily traffic histogram
Schedule pilot scoping call for dedicated vs hosted decision (week of 2026-05-04)
action_items: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE): upload parity-mapping spreadsheet + console tour video; due 2026-05-01
Sana Patel (Redwood SE): run perf bench (latency and token cost) with Prism sample prompts on Redwood hosted and dedicated configs; due 2026-05-06
Alex Chang (Prism CTO): share 3 core prompt templates, token length distribution, peak QPS estimate; due 2026-05-04
Samir Patel (Prism Security): confirm data residency needs and any paused/legal review windows; due 2026-05-05
summary: Introductory kickoff to align on porting sprint from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood. Covered architecture, security constraints (KMS, VPC, SOC2), performance expectations, parity mapping approach, and next steps for a short pilot. AE+SE committed to benchmark and share docs; customer to provide prompt set and traffic profile.
topics: Introductions; Current stack & constraints; Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC); Parity mapping strategy; Console & Optimize walkthrough; Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; Pilot scope and next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for making time — Jordan from Redwood here. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Alex Chang: Alex, Prism Labs, CTO. Hey Jordan.
[00:08] Maya Rivera: Maya, platform engineering. Good morning.
[00:10] Samir Patel: Samir, security. Hi all.
[00:12] Jordan Meyers: Great. Sana is on as the SE. Sana, want to intro?
[00:15] Sana Patel: Yep hi, Sana Patel, infra and perf at Redwood, I'll be driving the benchmarks and the console tour later.
[00:19] Jordan Meyers: Cool, agenda — quick discovery of what you're running now, then a parity mapping approach, then console/Optimize walkthrough and wrap with explicit next steps.
[00:30] Alex Chang: Sounds good. Quick background — we've been running a mixed stack: OpenAI for most chat endpoints, Anthropic for more safety-critical assistant flows, and a few endpoints on Together for internal R&D. We want to consolidate to reduce vendor overhead and improve latency predictability. Main asks: comparable output quality, similar latency at peak, and no regression in safety filters.
[00:50] Jordan Meyers: Great, that tracks. When you say "peak"—what are we talking? QPS, token lengths?
[00:56] Maya Rivera: Peak is around 120 QPS across all regions, token lengths average 350, tail up to 1,200 tokens for long form. We also have bursts to 220 for short periods.
[01:10] Sana Patel: Okay that's helpful. On Redwood side we can route by region and tier, and we have both hosted and dedicated options. For those tail long sequences we can recommend quantized variants and prefix caching to keep cost down.
[01:24] Samir Patel: Security — we need SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS with customer-managed keys for embeddings and logs. Also data residency in eu-west-1 for some PII flows. Can Redwood support that?
[01:37] Jordan Meyers: Short answer yes — Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem and KMS integrations. Hosted can be configured with customer-managed KMS and region pinning in some cases; for strict residency we'd recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll share SOC2 pack and the KMS integration guide after the call.
[01:51] Alex Chang: Are the audit logs tamper-evident? We need long-term retention for compliance.
[01:55] Sana Patel: We provide immutable audit logs for Private deployments; Hosted has audit trails and can export to your SIEM — retention tiers are an add-on. We'll put exact retention/format in the doc.
[02:08] Jordan Meyers: Let's talk parity mapping — typically we map the API calls and prompts to model variants in Redwood, test generation equivalence on a sample prompt set, and quantify deltas in both quality and unit cost. We do a small canary and rollback plan.
[02:24] Alex Chang: We have a parity spreadsheet already for OpenAI -> Anthropic differences, can we use that?
[02:29] Jordan Meyers: Yes please, share it. We'll add a column for Redwood model mapping and expected latency/cost. I'll upload a template after this call (link will be in the follow-up).
[02:40] Rita Gomez: For the safety-critical flows, we need to preserve Anthropic-style safety behavior. Is there an easy mapping?
[02:46] Sana Patel: Good question. There's no 1:1 always — we use prompt engineering + model variant tuning and sometimes light post-filtering. We'll propose an equivalent model and a set of guard rails; for RLHF-style safety differences we can run A/B tests during the pilot.
[02:59] Alex Chang: Curious about the console — can we see token-level cost per route?
[03:03] Sana Patel: Yes, Console shows token breakdown by route and model. We'll show the cost-per-response view and the Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization).
[03:12] Jordan Meyers: Demo time — Sana will share screen for a short console tour, then we'll switch to Optimize.
[03:20] [Screen share starts, faint cross-talk]
[03:25] Sana Patel: Alright, this is the Redwood Console — top left is the model catalog, you can pin model versions per route. Here's a sample route mapping, routing policy to prefer low-latency tier, fallback to cheaper variant. Sorry if the resolution is low — my VPN's a bit slow.
[03:42] Maya Rivera: Can we create rules by endpoint path? We have /chat, /summarize, etc.
[03:46] Sana Patel: Yep, per-route configs. You can set batching windows, max tokens, streaming on/off, and custom routing. Also you can attach monitoring profiles and regression alerts.
[03:56] Jordan Meyers: Note: prefix caching is automatic for repeated prefixes across users — can shave a lot off token cost for short repeated prompts.
[04:05] Alex Chang: How does prefix caching interact with privacy? We can't cache PII.
[04:09] Sana Patel: Good call — caching can be opt-out per route and we also support exclusion rules. For PII flows we'd disable cache or use only KV cache with in-tenant encryption.
[04:20] Samir Patel: KMS integration specifics — do you support customer-managed keys in hosted? We need envelope encryption for embeddings.
[04:27] Sana Patel: Hosted supports CMEK for embeddings and logs in regions that allow it; Private gives you full control. We'll include the KMS guide. There can be limitations depending on cloud provider.
[04:40] Alex Chang: On the perf side, can Redwood match Together's low-latency GPU instances for our short chat flows?
[04:46] Sana Patel: We have specialized attention kernels and continuous batching to reduce latencies. For sub-100ms token latencies we often recommend Dedicated capacity on a GPU family we tuned. We'll validate with benchmarks.
[04:59] Jordan Meyers: For cost — Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per model and mixed-precision where we see minimal quality impact. That usually gives a 2-4x token cost reduction depending on workload.
[05:12] Alex Chang: That sounds promising. We'll need sample numbers against our prompt set.
[05:17] Jordan Meyers: Right. Sana will run the 48-hour baseline and return per-endpoint cost estimates.
[05:23] Rita Gomez: Any gotchas moving from function-calling on OpenAI — we use structured tool calls in several flows.
[05:30] Sana Patel: Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured outputs; some models have slightly different behavior but we preserve the same streaming and JSON-schema enforcement. We'll include example payloads.
[05:40] Alex Chang: Can we do canary routing by user segment? We want 5% of production traffic to hit Redwood initially.
[05:45] Sana Patel: Yes — we support percentage-based rollouts and canary + automatic fallback if error rates cross thresholds.
[05:52] Jordan Meyers: Ok quick security recap before demo ends — we'll send SOC2 + KMS docs, and Samir will flag any further compliance needs.
[06:00] Samir Patel: I also want to see pen-test/attestation info and your incident response timelines.
[06:05] Jordan Meyers: We'll include IR timelines and contact list in the security pack.
[06:09] [Brief pause]
[06:12] Sana Patel: Back to Optimize — here are sample recommendations: lower batching for low-latency routes, enable prefix caching for chat starters, set conservative cache TTL for user-scoped prompts, and apply int8 quantization for long-form generation models. These are tunable per-route.
[06:30] Maya Rivera: For quantization, any accuracy regressions we should expect?
[06:34] Sana Patel: Minor in some cases. We run A/B on quality metrics and flag regressions via the Console. It's rare for customer-facing flows to degrade if we pick the right profile.
[06:45] Alex Chang: Let's talk timeline — we want a 6-week pilot to validate parity and cost savings, then decide on Dedicated vs Hosted by end of Q2. Is that realistic?
[06:54] Jordan Meyers: That's reasonable. Week 1: parity mapping + bench; Week 2–3: pilot deployment and monitoring; Week 4–6: user validation and safety checks. We'll sync weekly.
[07:07] Rita Gomez: Who will own the pilot infra on Redwood's side?
[07:10] Jordan Meyers: Sana will be SE lead and Jordan will be AE lead. We'll also loop in Solutions Eng if needed.
[07:18] [Short crosstalk]
[07:22] Alex Chang: A couple of edge questions — can we run hybrid routing so certain endpoints stay on Anthropic for safety and others move?
[07:28] Sana Patel: Absolutely — hybrid routing is a standard pattern. You can pin specific endpoints or user segments to another vendor and route the rest to Redwood. We also provide split sample rates for A/B.
[07:38] Samir Patel: About logs — do you redact PII automatically before logs leave our VPC?
[07:44] Sana Patel: We have redaction hooks; in Private deployments you can enforce a pre-export redaction lambda. In Hosted we provide configurable redaction and recommend customer-side tokenization for sensitive flows.
[07:57] Jordan Meyers: Any final objections or blockers we should know about?
[08:02] Alex Chang: Main blocker is proving parity on the safety flows and a clear cost model. If those check out, consent from procurement is straightforward.
[08:10] Jordan Meyers: Understood. We'll prioritize the safety parity tests and the cost baseline.
[08:15] Maya Rivera: Also, we will need the contract terms around retention and data deletion.
[08:20] Jordan Meyers: We'll include standard deletion SLAs and custom retention options in the follow-up.
[08:25] [Meeting moves to closing]
[08:28] Jordan Meyers: Quick recap of next steps — Jordan shares docs and parity template; Sana runs bench; Prism shares prompts and traffic. We schedule the pilot scoping for early May. Any other items?
[08:40] Rita Gomez: Could you also send an example canary policy?
[08:43] Sana Patel: Yep will attach.
[08:45] Alex Chang: Great thanks everyone.
[08:47] Jordan Meyers: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the pack. Meeting end.
[08:50] [Call ended]
